tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent with explicit trigger phrases like 'why is my CloudTrail bill so high', 'reduce CloudTrail costs', and lists concrete trigger contexts covering various user-facing scenarios. It briefly mentions implementation (read-only APIs) but this is secondary and concise overall.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when a user asks to reduce, review, audit, or optimize CloudTrail spend, or reports an unexpected CloudTrail cost or usage increase. Activate on requests like \"why is my CloudTrail bill so high\", \"reduce CloudTrail costs\", \"find duplicate CloudTrail trails\"..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is focused on domain-specific facts (CloudTrail billing model, opportunity checks, safety boundaries) rather than explaining general AWS/CloudTrail concepts the agent would already know. It stays concise and directs detailed material to reference files.
tests.evidence: Management events: the first copy per Region is free; every additional copy is billed. Data events: every copy is billed, including the first

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body summarizes the billing model briefly and defers full charge tables, API details, and opportunity check definitions to references/ files rather than embedding large blocks or detailed conditional logic.
tests.evidence: For the full charge-by-charge table and the detailed billing consequences the checks rely on, load references/billing-model.md

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Each of the three references files is linked with a markdown link in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies a clear trigger condition for when to load it, e.g. deciding whether a copy is free/paid, or performing inventory/analysis steps.
tests.evidence: load references/billing-model.md when you need to decide whether a specific trail copy is free or paid, or to explain a charge.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root in the correct 'references/filename.md' format.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/compliance-sensitive operations (safety boundaries, dedup-vs-filtering rule) are given exact prescriptive rules, while flexible tasks (scope selection, usage signal collection) explain reasoning and allow agent judgment.
tests.evidence: Never recommend reducing the single authoritative security trail below the organization's logging requirements. When in doubt, recommend converting a duplicate to data-events-only rather than deleting it.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: When multiple usage/volume signals are listed, Cost Explorer is explicitly designated as the preferred/default signal with others as fallbacks.
tests.evidence: This is the most direct dollar signal — prefer it when the role has Cost Explorer access.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (scope identification, inventory, usage signal collection, analysis, validation, reporting) applicable to any CloudTrail cost review, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Identify target scope. Ask the user which accounts and Regions to review...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated 'Known Quirks' section with concrete, non-obvious corrections (free copy rule, shadow trails, dedup-vs-filtering exclusivity).
tests.evidence: Organizations trails appear as shadow trails in member accounts — set includeShadowTrails=true and do not double-count them as member-created duplicates.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides an explicit report template asset for its report-generation purpose.
tests.evidence: Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure, section order, and table schemas in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md).

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline templates exist in the body; the report template is stored in assets/ and referenced conditionally, and the severity table is short.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file report-template.md is linked in the body.
tests.evidence: [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Load that template when generating the report.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies the trigger: generating the final report.
tests.evidence: Load that template when generating the report.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a correct relative path from skill root.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The workflow is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labels, matching required format.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 5 explicitly instructs the agent to self-check findings for double-counting and validate that dollar estimates trace to cited signals before writing the report.
tests.evidence: Step 5: Validate findings. Before writing the report, self-check the findings: confirm no finding double-counts savings already captured by a §4.1 dedup...
